item.title: Two Minute Papers — 'DeepSeek Solved AI’s Memory Problem'
item.body: Károly Zsolnai-Fehér explains DeepSeek's idea of storing long text as images to save tokens.
item.article_text:
Two Minute Papers · 2026-10-11 · notable
Two Minute Papers — 'DeepSeek Solved AI’s Memory Problem'
Two Minute Papers covers DeepSeek-OCR, DeepSeek's open MIT-licensed model that packs a page of text into as few as 64 vision tokens, an idea DeepSeek calls contexts optical compression.
Károly Zsolnai-Fehér explains DeepSeek's idea of storing long text as images to save tokens.
What is it?
'DeepSeek Solved AI’s Memory Problem' went up on Two Minute Papers on 11 October 2026. The video description names the DeepSeek-OCR GitHub repository as its source paper.
How does it work?
DeepSeek-OCR renders text as an image and reads it back through a vision encoder, so a page costs a fixed number of vision tokens: 64 at 512×512, 100 at 640×640, 256 at 1024×1024 and 400 at 1280×1280. DeepSeek reports about 2,500 tokens per second for PDF processing on one A100-40G with vLLM.
Why does it matter?
Long contexts are expensive because every text token costs memory and compute. Compressing old context into a small number of vision tokens is one way to let a model keep more history for less, which is the 'memory problem' the video title refers to.
Who is it for?
anyone curious about long-context LLMs

item.title: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo — Qwen's image model now draws and edits in 8 steps
item.body: The fast version of Qwen-Image-2.1: the same 7B image generator and editor, cut to 8 denoising steps.
item.article_text:
Alibaba (Qwen) · 2026-10-09 · notable
Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo — Qwen's image model now draws and edits in 8 steps
Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo is an accelerated checkpoint of Alibaba's 7B Qwen-Image-2.1. It generates and edits images in 8 denoising steps with CFG=1. Weights are on Hugging Face under the research-only Qwen license, with Pro and Turbo APIs live.
The fast version of Qwen-Image-2.1: the same 7B image generator and editor, cut to 8 denoising steps.
What is it?
Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo is a faster checkpoint of Qwen-Image-2.1, the 7B image model Qwen released on 20 September. One model still covers text-to-image, single-image edits, multi-reference composition and transparent RGBA output. The same day, Qwen made Qwen-Image-2.1 Pro and Turbo available as APIs on Alibaba Cloud Model Studio.
How does it work?
The speed comes from the step count: Turbo runs 8 denoising steps with CFG=1 by default, while the base model's quickstart uses 40. It also reuses text and reference-image context across steps with prefix KV caching. The checkpoint carries its own 8-step schedule, so changing `num_inference_steps` alone does not override it, and Qwen says other schedules are not evaluated.
Why does it matter?
Fewer steps means faster and cheaper images on your own GPU, which matters most for editing loops where you try many variants. The catch from the base model stays: the weights are under the Qwen Research License, so commercial products need separate terms or the hosted API.
Who is it for?
researchers and hobbyists running image generation locally
Try it
Load Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo with the diffusers QwenImage21Pipeline (diffusers from source, transformers>=5.17.0).

item.title: 226 review-loop 2dmurali/review-loop-skill 1.6K
item.body:
review-loop
Review Loop
Iterative worker-reviewer cycle within a single session. You do the work, spawn a reviewer subagent to critique it, revise based on feedback, repeat until quality gate is met.
Core principle: First drafts are never final. Iterative critique produces better output than a single pass.
Platform note: This skill works best with agents that support subagent spawning. On platforms without that capability, simulate the reviewer step by opening a fresh chat context, pasting only the work product (no prior reasoning), and asking it to score 1-10 with specific feedback.
Quick Start
- Say: "implement X, use review-loop" or"run review-loop on the file I just wrote"
- The agent does the work (or reads existing work)
- A separate critic subagent scores it 1-10 with specific feedback
- The agent revises and repeats until score >= 8 (default quality gate)
- A loop summary is delivered with the final output

item.title: Apple TV 4K (4th Gen) Launches with Siri AI, A19 Chip, and Hands-Free Control
item.body: Source: apple.com | Added to Future Tools: 2026-10-13T16:10:10.398Z | Release date: 2026-10-13 | Paywalled: no
item.article_text:
PRESS RELEASE
                    
                    
                        October 13, 2026
                    
                    
                
            Apple unveils the new Apple TV 4K, supercharged by Siri AI
                
                
                    A more capable and conversational Siri, faster performance, and an even more immersive home theater setup elevate the entertainment experience
                
            
        CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today announced the next generation of Apple TV 4K, delivering its most immersive home theater experience yet. The new Apple TV 4K features Siri AI, an entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence, transforming how users search for, discover, and enjoy their favorite movies and TV shows through a full-screen Siri AI experience.1 With built-in far-field microphones, Apple TV 4K also lets users talk to Siri completely hands-free.2
                 
             
                 The new Apple TV 4K delivers even faster performance and, when paired with four HomePod mini 2 or HomePod (2nd generation) speakers, unlocks the most immersive home theater surround sound setup Apple has ever offered. As a home hub, Apple TV 4K also makes managing the smart home easier than ever, with Apple Intelligence-generated camera activity descriptions and summarized notifications in the Home app, and control of accessories and scenes.3
                 
             
                 The new Apple TV 4K can be pre-ordered starting today, with availability beginning November 13.
                 
             
                 “The new Apple TV 4K is our most immersive home theater experience yet,” said Bob Borchers, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Product Marketing. “With Siri AI, finding something to watch becomes a full-screen, conversational experience, and with built-in far-field microphones, it’s completely hands-free. Pair it with HomePod for the best surround sound setup we’ve ever offered, and it makes managing your Apple Home accessories easier than ever. Now, alongside HomeView, HomePod mini 2, and Apple Home Collection, it’s part of the most connected Apple Home we’ve ever built.”
                 
             
                 An Entirely New Version of Siri Powered by Apple Intelligence
Apple TV 4K brings Siri AI to the living room with a rich, full-screen experience. An entirely new version of Siri powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence, Siri AI is a profoundly more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, and the ability to take even more systemwide app actions, making it effortless to find entertainment. Users can simply ask Siri “What Apple TV shows won at the Emmy Awards this year?” and see beautiful poster art pulled directly from the Apple TV app, along with relevant suggestions like “More award-winning comedies” to keep exploring. While watching, users can ask Siri AI follow-up questions and tap into Siri AI’s broad world knowledge to go deeper into a show, asking things like “Where was Pluribus filmed?” or “Is this appropriate for a 15-year-old?” Responses appear in a compact, subtle overlay, providing helpful information when viewers ask while keeping them immersed in the action. With an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone, Siri AI on Apple TV 4K can now tap into a user’s personal context to answer requests like “Play the show Alinda recommended.”
                 
             
         A Fully Hands-Free Experience with Far-Field Microphones
The new Apple TV 4K features three far-field microphones, letting users control what they’re watching and discover new shows completely hands-free. Advanced echo cancellation intelligently isolates a user’s voice from background sound to deliver crystal-clear “Hey Siri” or “Siri” recognition, even while audio is playing.
                 
             
         Faster Performance, Smarter Remote
The A19 chip in the new Apple TV 4K delivers up to 50 percent faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance than the previous generation, for greater responsiveness, faster navigation, and smoother animations. The A19 chip also includes a new, dedicated AV1 decoder, enabling more efficient, high-quality streaming while using less bandwidth.
                 
             
                 The new Siri Remote keeps its familiar design while adding Find My support with Precision Finding and an option to play a sound on the remote — making it far easier to locate.4
                 
             
         Apple’s Most Immersive Home Theater Ever
Pairing HomePod with Apple TV 4K already offers users an immersive viewing experience that’s easy to set up, and the new Apple TV 4K takes it even further. For the first time, users can create a four-speaker surround sound experience with Apple TV 4K (4th generation) and HomePod mini 2. The four speakers work together with Apple TV 4K to intelligently recognize their position in the room so audio timing and levels are automatically calibrated to the space. HomePod (2nd generation) can also be used in this four-speaker setup for the ultimate audio experience, as long as the front and rear speaker pairs match.5
                 
             
         An Even Smarter Home Hub
The new Apple TV 4K continues to serve as a powerful home hub, giving users control of their smart home accessories from anywhere.6 With a compatible doorbell, notifications appear directly on the TV so users can see who’s at the door, speak with them, and control other accessories like unlocking the door — all without interrupting what they’re watching. Apple TV 4K supports automations, guest mode, and secure local processing of HomeKit Secure Video, now enhanced with Apple Intelligence-generated camera activity video descriptions and summarized notifications. Users can also use Siri AI to control smart home accessories and turn scenes on or off

item.title: Apple HomeView Smart Display Launches at $299 with Siri AI and Facial Recognition
item.body: Source: theverge.com | Added to Future Tools: 2026-10-13T16:21:09.417Z | Release date: 2026-10-13 | Paywalled: no
item.article_text:
It’s finally here: Apple’s long-rumored smart display, the Apple HomeView, has arrived. I got a first look at the device in New York City this week, and it’s gorgeous. The HomeView puts a small, vibrant screen atop a speaker base for taking video calls, beautifully displaying photos, and providing information at a glance with Apple’s Siri AI voice assistant. The device’s square shape makes it feel less imposing than larger smart displays like Google’s Nest Hub Max or Amazon’s Echo Show 11, and I can see it fitting nicely on my kitchen counter — though it might be a hair too big for my bedside table.
Apple launches HomeView, its first smart display for the home
As Apple debuts Siri AI in the home, it’s focusing on a beautiful, multipurpose screen (and hiding your text messages from your kids), rather than innovative new smart home features.
The HomeView is the centerpiece of Apple’s new push into the home. It costs $299 and launches alongside a new collection of cameras, thermostats, and a door lock designed for Apple Home. As a smart home hub, Matter controller, and Thread Border Router, the HomeView can orchestrate these and other Apple Home and Matter smart home devices. It’s available in eight countries at launch: the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, South Africa, and India. Preorders are open now, with devices shipping November 13th.
The new smart display has Siri AI built in, enabling natural-language voice interactions to ask general knowledge questions, control smart home devices via voice and touch, and get information using personal context from your text messages, calendar, and emails. Personal context requires facial recognition and for your Apple Intelligence-capable iPhone to be on the same network, so your kids can’t peek at your texts over breakfast.
The HomeView can display neatly formatted recipes for following along as you cook, keep you in the picture on FaceTime video calls with Center Stage, and show live feeds and footage from HomeKit Secure Video cameras.
The HomeView’s 7-inch square screen sits atop a surprisingly small aluminum speaker base, attached by an adjustable stainless steel arm. It has no physical volume or power buttons, and no cover for the 12-megapixel FaceTime camera, which Apple says is used only for video calls and facial recognition.
The screen offers a variety of customizable “faces” that feel more like a big Apple Watch than a small iPad. When idle, the HomeView can display photo faces, clock faces, and Snoopy faces, or you can use a modular face to show widgets from your most-used apps, such as your to-do list, world clock, and podcasts. A home widget face offers controls for lights, climate, cameras, and other devices.
I haven’t had a chance to try the device yet, but I saw a demo showing how swiping up from the bottom of the screen pulls up a familiar app grid with Apple’s core apps — like Messages and Apple Music — all available.
Apple also showed a video demoing how it envisions a family of five using the HomeView around the kitchen counter during the morning rush. From pulling up a French toast recipe for breakfast to checking the calendar for the day to receiving a FaceTime call to asking it to find lost keys, Apple pictures the HomeView stepping in to help with common minor household crises.
The video shows the daughter sending a text message to her secret boyfriend from the HomeView, and the younger brother being foiled from attempting to read it because it shuts off when it doesn’t see her face, and then everyone views a live feed of said boyfriend arriving at the front door. The most unrealistic part of the video is that no one is holding an iPhone.
I’ve always seen smart displays as a good option for controlling smart home devices without having to pull out my phone and open an app. Apple’s vision for the HomeView takes that to its natural conclusion: you don’t have to pull out your phone for anything when you’re home since it’s all available on the HomeView (well, at least all of Apple’s apps). It’s an iPhone for your home.
The HomeView comes in four colors: silver, starlight, rose pink, and space gray. It features two speaker drivers in the display, plus a woofer and two force-canceling passive radiators in the base for bass. Based on initial listening, the sound hits a few notches above the HomePod Mini but doesn’t compete with the HomePod.
There’s a wall-mountable version without the speaker base that also costs $299 and comes with three mounting options: plug-in, in-wall power, and in-wall PoE. Apple says the audio is tuned for wall placement, but I didn’t get to hear it in action.
The screen is wrapped in an aluminum case and has no physical buttons; the frame is just dotted with a speaker grille and microphone holes. It has a Liquid Retina display — that usually means LCD in Apple’s language, though the company didn’t clarify — with True Tone support and ambient light adjustment, and it can go up to a bright 500 nits and down to a super-low 0.3 nits, which Apple says makes it usable as a bedside clock. The screen is large enough to see clearly from across the room but doesn’t adjust as you approach. You tap widgets to access different apps and controls, or use voice to tell it what to do.
While the HomeView functions as an Apple Home Hub — it enables local control of supported devices, creation of scenes and automations, and support for HomeKit Secure Video — the device feels less like a focused smart home controller and more like a way to use your iPhone less when you’re at home.
The HomeView supports a number of Apple’s own apps, including Calendar, Reminders, Messages, and Music. Apple says it also works with third-party audio and video apps that support the CarPlay architecture. A few audio apps, such as Spotify and Audible, are available, but no video apps yet.
Siri AI on HomeView is the same voice assistant as the upgraded version that arrived on the iPhone with iOS 27. It has no smart display-specific

item.body: We’re giving developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers access to Gemini 4 Argon, our latest frontier model.
item.article_text:
Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available today for developers and enterprises via the API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, for Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, and Google AI Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.
Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains, ranking #1 on the Vals Index, which measures model performance across critical economic sectors like finance, coding, legal, and tax work.
The model launches today at an introductory price 1 of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (with cached input tokens at 95% off).
Teams at Google, across enterprises, and in the research community have already been using Argon to land significant impact across fields:
- To solve major engineering problems like large codebase refactoring and optimizations
- To optimize business workflows across domains like legal, finance, and science
- To find and patch critical cybersecurity vulnerabilities
- To enable novel breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and life sciences
Solving complex engineering tasks
At Google, we’ve been using Argon on our hardest engineering problems. Over the past few weeks, software engineers have been shipping high-quality code faster than ever. Argon in Antigravity has helped teams increase agentic code submissions by more than 35% while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third.
- Untangling browser feature code in Chrome: Argon helped the Chrome team separate core webpage handling from a ~6 million line legacy folder of browser features held within Chromium’s 40 million-line codebase. Piping multiple clean code changes at a time, Argon helped the team finish an architectural refactor across hundreds of files, completing months of work in weeks. For Chrome's billions of global users, this will unlock the ability for live webpages to move fluidly between tabs, side panels, and floating windows without reloading, eliminating an entire category of browser crashes.
- Optimizing a production Python codebase in hours: Argon in Antigravity is helping the team behind Google's open-source Agent Development Kit (ADK), a framework powering enterprise agents, push their performance engineering further. The team gave Argon their .agents/skills rulebook and a one-paragraph goal to eliminate framework overhead without breaking existing apps. Working autonomously overnight, Argon surfaced optimizations, now live in google/adk-python, that cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and sped up cold imports by 21%. Read the engineering deep dive to learn more.
- Quantum chemistry open-source package optimization: xTB (Semiempirical Extended Tight-Binding) is one of the most-cited open-source quantum chemistry packages for molecules. Scientists use it to predict molecules' 3D shapes and to screen large numbers of drug and materials candidates. Using Argon in Antigravity, our researchers made xTB up to 2.3x faster at predicting molecular structures and 1.8x faster at conformer search. The changes have been contributed to the official xTB repository on GitHub.
- Making our open Gemma models nearly three times as fast: Using Argon, we achieved a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on an A100 via vLLM (accelerating throughput from ~37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second on Gemma 4 E2B) with 100% token parity and zero quality drop in just a few days, a process that would usually take months. Check out the upstream pull requests (optimizing everything from attention tuning to speculative decoding) to see the exact changes.
- Delivering complex 3D visualizations: Argon brings major improvements in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding compared to previous Gemini models. Using slash commands like /goal and prompting for multi-agent loops with custom skills in Antigravity, Googlers are using Argon to prototype complex 3D visualizations, high-fidelity games, and interactive animations in vanilla code that can be rendered directly in the browser.
Transforming critical business and professional workflows
Argon combines frontier reasoning, deep visual perception, expanded domain knowledge, and stronger writing capabilities across legal, finance, science, and coding to help with high-stakes professional workflows. It communicates clearly, keeping you in the loop, and follows style instructions better than any of our previous Gemini models. Argon answers questions more directly with less hedging, doesn’t repeat itself more than necessary, and skips clichés throughout the responses.
Enterprise customers and startups in our early access program are already seeing strong wins with Argon.
Using its advanced reasoning and multimodal capabilities while maintaining strict grounding, Argon excels in deep multimodal document comprehension, longitudinal data analysis, and interactive analytical sandboxes.
Accelerating real-world impact with researchers and domain experts
Researchers, engineers, and security specialists are already using Argon to push the boundaries of cyber defense, science, math, and robotics. It’s helping cyber defenders and researchers test hypotheses, autonomously audit critical codebases and formal proofs, and catch subtle zero-day vulnerabilities and logic flaws.

item.title: Fireship — 'Every app on Earth is now open source... whether it likes it or not'
item.body: Fireship looks at what happens when one developer and a coding model can clone a whole commercial software suite.
item.article_text:
Fireship · 2026-10-12 · notable
Fireship — 'Every app on Earth is now open source... whether it likes it or not'
Fireship's 12 October 2026 video covers a developer who rewrote seven Adobe apps in Rust with help from Claude Opus 5.5 and released them as open source for free.
Fireship looks at what happens when one developer and a coding model can clone a whole commercial software suite.
What is it?
'Every app on Earth is now open source... whether it likes it or not' went up on Fireship on 12 October 2026. The description says 'a developer just rewrote seven Adobe apps in Rust and open-sourced them for free' and invites viewers to try them.
How does it work?
XDA Developers reports that a developer with about a decade of Rust experience built open-source versions of Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign and Acrobat Pro, announcing the seven apps as 'created with the help of Opus 5.5'.
Why does it matter?
If a strong coding model lets one person rebuild large commercial apps, the moat around paid desktop software gets thinner. That is the claim in the video's title, and it is a live question for anyone who sells software.
Who is it for?
developers and software founders
